symptom: Three untrusted Forward v0.2 assessment APIs (authority metadata, trust-policy preflight, and cross-envelope authority batch) returned writable objects and writable blocker arrays even though their TypeScript types declared literal false authorization. A consumer holding a returned result could mutate scoringAuthorized or independentAuthorityVerified at runtime and alter blockers without re-running the structural checks. This is an output-integrity gap in research-only metadata, not proof of independent evidence or a production admission path.
lesson: Compile-time readonly and literal false fields do not prevent a runtime consumer from rewriting a deny-only research assessment. Even a correct preflight can hand off a mutable object whose flags and denial reasons no longer reflect its actual result.
guardrail: Freeze every returned deny-only assessment object and its blocker array at the return boundary. Regression-test both consistent-but-unverified and rejected paths by attempting to mutate authority flags and blocker arrays; require TypeError and preserved false flags. This protects research metadata only and does not authenticate evidence, grant scoring, or connect production.
